correctness.rationale: For every α>-1 the normalized weighted half-plane kernel has derivatives (∂_z^r∂_{bar w}^s K)/K=(-1)^r(h)_{r+s}(z-bar w)^(-r-s). Expanding the nine real-coefficient terms cancels odd powers and yields the quartic t^4+(h)_2(2b-a²)t²+(h)_4b². For b≠0, C=(h)_2(2b-a²) is strictly below 2sqrt(E), E=(h)_4b²>0. Its two u=t² roots are positive real exactly when C≤-2sqrt(E), including a positive double root at equality, and otherwise form a nonreal conjugate pair. Exactly one square root from each nonreal u lies in Im t>0, giving two distinct simple scalar zeros; every such t is achieved by an interior pair z,w. The b=0 factorization has only real t roots. This proves necessity, sufficiency and sharpness, while 414 finite test configurations plus an independent symbolic nine-term polynomial identity checked signs and normalization. Numerical tests do not establish the universal result.

value.rationale: This is a complete sharp classification for the simplest real symmetric functional with three consecutive nonzero derivative coefficients, not an arbitrary isolated example. In contrast to the known unavoidable zeros for separated order-zero/order-two jets, a sufficiently strong first-order term removes every off-diagonal kernel zero. The exact zero-free cone, two-scalar-zero complement, double-root phase boundary, and asymmetric weight dependence identify structural information relevant to Lu Qi-Keng phenomena and stable differential sampling that neither covered two-term case supplies.
